messages.content:
You are a quantitative social scientist adding a small set of EXPLORATORY analyses (at most three) to a survey experiment whose registered tests are already done. Choose analyses that help interpret the registered results: e.g. effects on component items, robustness to attention-check failures or alternative exclusions, heterogeneity by a demographic the PAP did not register, dose/manipulation checks, or a placebo. Avoid fishing; each analysis must have a one-sentence rationale.

Write ONE script scripts/04_exploratory.py (pandas, statsmodels, matplotlib Agg) that reads data/clean.csv, writes one tidy CSV per analysis to results/E<k>_<slug>.csv and at most two PNG figures to figures/ (minimal style: white background, no top/right/left spines, no gridlines, dark ink, one accent colour at most, direct labels instead of legends, 200 dpi), and prints one summary line per analysis. Use HC2 robust SEs. Run it with run_script; fix errors; then call
record_result(key="exploratory", value=[{"id":"E1","title":str,"rationale":str,"method":str,"table":"results/E1_x.csv","figure":"figures/..png" or null,"finding":one sentence with the key number}], final=true).
Reuse the registered script's helpers instead of writing your own model code. At the top of your script:
    import importlib.util, pathlib
    _spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
Then `formula, d2 = reg.build_formula(outcome, est, covariates, df_subset)` and `res = reg.fit(d2, formula, est)` give exactly the registered model (Lin centring, weights, HC2) on any subset; `reg.HYPOTHESES` holds each hypothesis dict with its `estimator` (use `est = h['estimator']`). For a plain weighted regression of your own, pass weights as a Series: `smf.wls(formula, data=d, weights=d['ipw']).fit(cov_type='HC2')` (never a column name string). Convert any object-typed numeric column with `pd.to_numeric(..., errors='coerce')` before fitting.
Robustness checks of a registered estimate must re-fit the SAME specification as scripts/03_registered.py (same formula, same weights column, same covariates and centring, same HC2 errors) on the alternative sample, and the table must hold both the original and the re-estimated estimate and SE side by side. If a standard error changes by more than a factor of two while the sample changes by less than 10%, your model is misspecified: fix it or drop the analysis.
Never print rows of data. Do not read data files directly.

You have 12 turns. Turn 1: write_file the full script. Turn 2: run_script. Fix and re-run if needed, then record_result with final=true. Record whatever analyses succeeded before you run out of turns.

## Design

## Registered hypotheses (already tested)
- H1: AMCE of information type on sharing: each level against 'True/neutral', from the regression of sharing on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent. (outcome share)
- H2: AMCE of tie strength on sharing: each level against 'Distant tie', from the regression of sharing on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent. (outcome share)

- H8: AMCE of information type on plausibility: each level against 'True/neutral', from the regression of plausibility on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent. (outcome plausibility)

- H14: AMCE of sharer belief in disputed claims on plausibility: each level against 'Conspiracy belief: low', from the regression of plausibility on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent. (outcome plausibility)

- R2: AMCE of sharer origin on sharing: each level against 'Foreign origin', from the regression of sharing on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent; re-weighted by the inverse of the realized assignment probability of sharer origin (stabilized). (outcome share)

- R11: AMCE of sharer political knowledge on plausibility: each level against 'Knowledge: low', from the regression of plausibility on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent; re-weighted by the inverse of the realized assignment probability of sharer political knowledge (stabilized). (outcome plausibility)
- R12: AMCE of sharer belief in disputed claims on plausibility: each level against 'Conspiracy belief: low', from the regression of plausibility on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent; re-weighted by the inverse of the realized assignment probability of sharer belief in disputed claims (stabilized). (outcome plausibility)
- X1: A1. Source credibility is conditional on content uncertainty: the slope of sharing on trust in the sharer (1-5), net of the other source attributes, and how it differs by information type. (outcome share)
- X2: A1. The slope of plausibility on trust in the sharer, by information type. (outcome plausibility)
- X3: A1. The close-tie premium on sharing, net of the other source attributes, by information type. (outcome share)
- X4: A2. Sharing without believing: among profiles chosen to share, the probability that the respondent judged the other post more plausible, by information type, net of source attributes, media trust and age. (outcome share_not_believe)
- X5: A3. Co-ideological messenger: sharing when the respondent and the sharer lean the same way (both liberal or both conservative) against opposite leans; pairs involving a moderate form a third group. Cell differences, no controls. (outcome share)
- X6: A4. Ego-network composition: the respondent's six named contacts as a measured network. Among misinformation profiles, sharing on the network's mean perceived belief in disputed claims, net of network ideological spread, mean trust, age and ideology. Each misinformation profile is weighted by 1 / the respondent's number of them, which reproduces the respondent-level regression of the misinformation-sharing rate. (outcome share)
- X7: B1. Message x respondent congruence: among partisan respondents shown partisan-slanted headlines, sharing of congenial against uncongenial content (headline slant from the paper's preliminary automated coding), by information type. (outcome share)
- X8: B2. A conspiracy-prone source: the slope of sharing on the sharer's perceived belief in disputed claims (0-1), net of the other source attributes, by information type. (outcome share)
- X9: B2. The slope of plausibility on the sharer's perceived belief in disputed claims, by information type. (outcome plausibility)
- X10: B2, claim-specific (thin): for the anti-vaccine (polio) misinformation headline, plausibility when the sharer is seen as believing 'Covid-19 vaccines modify your DNA' against not. (outcome plausibility)
- X11: B3. Health vs. political misinformation: among misinformation profiles, the trust slope on sharing for health (guanabana, polio) and political headlines. (outcome share)
- X12: B3. Among misinformation profiles, the close-tie premium for health and political headlines. (outcome share)
- X13: B4. Sharer origin (continental US vs. elsewhere) and sharing, by survey language and by the respondent's nativity. (outcome share)

import importlib.util, pathlib
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/clean.csv')
H = [h for h in reg.HYPOTHESES if (h.get('id') or h.get('analysis_id')) == 'H1'][0]
est = H['estimator']; cov = H.get('covariates', [])

def amce(sub, arm='Misinformation'):
    f, d2 = reg.build_formula('share', est, cov, sub)
    r = reg.fit(d2, f, est)
    k = [i for i in r.params.index if 'arm_code' in i and arm in i][0]
    return float(r.params[k]), float(r.bse[k]), int(r.nobs)

orig = pd.read_csv('results/registered_summary.csv')
orig = orig[orig.analysis_id == 'H1:Misinformation'].iloc[0]

# E1: drop respondents who picked the same screen position in all trials
pos = df.assign(a=(df.profile == 'A').astype(float)).loc[df.chosen_share == 1]
g = pos.groupby('resp_id')['a'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
bad = g.index[(g['count'] >= 3) & (g['mean'].isin([0, 1]))]
sub = df[~df.resp_id.isin(bad)]
b, s, n = amce(sub)
e1 = pd.DataFrame([{'sample': 'registered', 'estimate': orig.estimate, 'se': orig.std_error, 'n': orig.n},
                   {'sample': 'drop position-straightliners', 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n}])
e1.to_csv('results/E1_straightliners.csv', index=False)
print(f'E1 misinfo AMCE {orig.estimate:.3f} -> {b:.3f} (se {orig.std_error:.3f}->{s:.3f}), dropped {len(bad)} resp')

# E2: heterogeneity by age tertile
rows = []
for t in ['Lowest', 'Middle', 'Highest']:
    for arm in ['Misinformation', 'Fact-check']:
        b, s, n = amce(df[df.age_t == t], arm)
        rows.append({'age_tertile': t, 'arm': arm, 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n})
e2 = pd.DataFrame(rows); e2.to_csv('results/E2_age_tertile.csv', index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), facecolor='white')
for arm, c, off in [('Misinformation', '#c0392b', -0.05), ('Fact-check', '#333333', 0.05)]:
    d = e2[e2.arm == arm]; x = np.arange(3) + off
    ax.errorbar(x, d.estimate, yerr=1.96 * d.se, fmt='o', color=c, capsize=0)
    ax.text(2.2, d.estimate.iloc[-1], arm, color=c, va='center')
ax.axhline(0, color='#333333', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(3)); ax.set_xticklabels(['Youngest', 'Middle', 'Oldest'])
ax.set_xlim(-0.4, 3.2); ax.set_ylabel('AMCE on sharing')
for sp in ['top', 'right', 'left']: ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('figures/E2_age_tertile.png', dpi=200)
m = e2[e2.arm == 'Misinformation'].estimate
print(f'E2 misinfo AMCE by age tertile: {m.round(3).tolist()}')

Among misinformation profiles, sharing on the network's mean perceived belief in disputed claims, net of network ideological spread, mean trust, age and ideology. function.arguments:
{"path": "scripts/04_exploratory.py", "content": "import importlib.util, pathlib
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/clean.csv')
H = [h for h in reg.HYPOTHESES if (h.get('id') or h.get('analysis_id')) == 'H1'][0]
est = H['estimator']; cov = H.get('covariates', [])

def amce(sub, arm='Misinformation'):
    f, d2 = reg.build_formula('share', est, cov, sub)
    r = reg.fit(d2, f, est)
    k = [i for i in r.params.index if 'arm_code' in i and arm in i][0]
    return float(r.params[k]), float(r.bse[k]), int(r.nobs)

orig = pd.read_csv('results/registered_summary.csv')
orig = orig[orig.analysis_id == 'H1:Misinformation'].iloc[0]

# E1: drop respondents who picked the same screen position in all trials
pos = df.assign(a=(df.profile == 'A').astype(float)).loc[df.chosen_share == 1]
g = pos.groupby('resp_id')['a'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
bad = g.index[(g['count'] >= 3) & (g['mean'].isin([0, 1]))]
sub = df[~df.resp_id.isin(bad)]
b, s, n = amce(sub)
e1 = pd.DataFrame([{'sample': 'registered', 'estimate': orig.estimate, 'se': orig.std_error, 'n': orig.n},
                   {'sample': 'drop position-straightliners', 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n}])
e1.to_csv('results/E1_straightliners.csv', index=False)
print(f'E1 misinfo AMCE {orig.estimate:.3f} -> {b:.3f} (se {orig.std_error:.3f}->{s:.3f}), dropped {len(bad)} resp')

# E2: heterogeneity by age tertile
rows = []
for t in ['Lowest', 'Middle', 'Highest']:
    for arm in ['Misinformation', 'Fact-check']:
        b, s, n = amce(df[df.age_t == t], arm)
        rows.append({'age_tertile': t, 'arm': arm, 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n})
e2 = pd.DataFrame(rows); e2.to_csv('results/E2_age_tertile.csv', index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), facecolor='white')
for arm, c, off in [('Misinformation', '#c0392b', -0.05), ('Fact-check', '#333333', 0.05)]:
    d = e2[e2.arm == arm]; x = np.arange(3) + off
    ax.errorbar(x, d.estimate, yerr=1.96 * d.se, fmt='o', color=c, capsize=0)
    ax.text(2.2, d.estimate.iloc[-1], arm, color=c, va='center')
ax.axhline(0, color='#333333', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(3)); ax.set_xticklabels(['Youngest', 'Middle', 'Oldest'])
ax.set_xlim(-0.4, 3.2); ax.set_ylabel('AMCE on sharing')
for sp in ['top', 'right', 'left']: ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('figures/E2_age_tertile.png', dpi=200)
m = e2[e2.arm == 'Misinformation'].estimate
print(f'E2 misinfo AMCE by age tertile: {m.round(3).tolist()}')
"}

function.description: Hand a structured result to the orchestrator. Set final=true when your task is complete.

messages.content:
You are a quantitative social scientist adding a small set of EXPLORATORY analyses (at most three) to a survey experiment whose registered tests are already done. Choose analyses that help interpret the registered results: e.g. effects on component items, robustness to attention-check failures or alternative exclusions, heterogeneity by a demographic the PAP did not register, dose/manipulation checks, or a placebo. Avoid fishing; each analysis must have a one-sentence rationale.

Write ONE script scripts/04_exploratory.py (pandas, statsmodels, matplotlib Agg) that reads data/clean.csv, writes one tidy CSV per analysis to results/E<k>_<slug>.csv and at most two PNG figures to figures/ (minimal style: white background, no top/right/left spines, no gridlines, dark ink, one accent colour at most, direct labels instead of legends, 200 dpi), and prints one summary line per analysis. Use HC2 robust SEs. Run it with run_script; fix errors; then call
record_result(key="exploratory", value=[{"id":"E1","title":str,"rationale":str,"method":str,"table":"results/E1_x.csv","figure":"figures/..png" or null,"finding":one sentence with the key number}], final=true).
Reuse the registered script's helpers instead of writing your own model code. At the top of your script:
    import importlib.util, pathlib
    _spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
Then `formula, d2 = reg.build_formula(outcome, est, covariates, df_subset)` and `res = reg.fit(d2, formula, est)` give exactly the registered model (Lin centring, weights, HC2) on any subset; `reg.HYPOTHESES` holds each hypothesis dict with its `estimator` (use `est = h['estimator']`). For a plain weighted regression of your own, pass weights as a Series: `smf.wls(formula, data=d, weights=d['ipw']).fit(cov_type='HC2')` (never a column name string). Convert any object-typed numeric column with `pd.to_numeric(..., errors='coerce')` before fitting.
Robustness checks of a registered estimate must re-fit the SAME specification as scripts/03_registered.py (same formula, same weights column, same covariates and centring, same HC2 errors) on the alternative sample, and the table must hold both the original and the re-estimated estimate and SE side by side. If a standard error changes by more than a factor of two while the sample changes by less than 10%, your model is misspecified: fix it or drop the analysis.
Never print rows of data. Do not read data files directly.

You have 12 turns. Turn 1: write_file the full script. Turn 2: run_script. Fix and re-run if needed, then record_result with final=true. Record whatever analyses succeeded before you run out of turns.

- X1: A1. Source credibility is conditional on content uncertainty: the slope of sharing on trust in the sharer (1-5), net of the other source attributes, and how it differs by information type. (outcome share)
- X2: A1. The slope of plausibility on trust in the sharer, by information type. (outcome plausibility)
- X3: A1. The close-tie premium on sharing, net of the other source attributes, by information type. (outcome share)
- X4: A2. Sharing without believing: among profiles chosen to share, the probability that the respondent judged the other post more plausible, by information type, net of source attributes, media trust and age. (outcome share_not_believe)
- X5: A3. Co-ideological messenger: sharing when the respondent and the sharer lean the same way (both liberal or both conservative) against opposite leans; pairs involving a moderate form a third group. Cell differences, no controls. (outcome share)
- X6: A4. Ego-network composition: the respondent's six named contacts as a measured network. Among misinformation profiles, sharing on the network's mean perceived belief in disputed claims, net of network ideological spread, mean trust, age and ideology. Each misinformation profile is weighted by 1 / the respondent's number of them, which reproduces the respondent-level regression of the misinformation-sharing rate. (outcome share)
- X7: B1. Message x respondent congruence: among partisan respondents shown partisan-slanted headlines, sharing of congenial against uncongenial content (headline slant from the paper's preliminary automated coding), by information type. (outcome share)
- X8: B2. A conspiracy-prone source: the slope of sharing on the sharer's perceived belief in disputed claims (0-1), net of the other source attributes, by information type. (outcome share)
- X9: B2. The slope of plausibility on the sharer's perceived belief in disputed claims, by information type. (outcome plausibility)
- X10: B2, claim-specific (thin): for the anti-vaccine (polio) misinformation headline, plausibility when the sharer is seen as believing 'Covid-19 vaccines modify your DNA' against not. (outcome plausibility)
- X11: B3. Health vs. political misinformation: among misinformation profiles, the trust slope on sharing for health (guanabana, polio) and political headlines. (outcome share)
- X12: B3. Among misinformation profiles, the close-tie premium for health and political headlines. (outcome share)
- X13: B4. Sharer origin (continental US vs. elsewhere) and sharing, by survey language and by the respondent's nativity. (outcome share)

{"path": "scripts/04_exploratory.py", "content": "import importlib.util, pathlib
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/clean.csv')
H = [h for h in reg.HYPOTHESES if (h.get('id') or h.get('analysis_id')) == 'H1'][0]
est = H['estimator']; cov = H.get('covariates', [])

def amce(sub, arm='Misinformation'):
    f, d2 = reg.build_formula('share', est, cov, sub)
    r = reg.fit(d2, f, est)
    k = [i for i in r.params.index if 'arm_code' in i and arm in i][0]
    return float(r.params[k]), float(r.bse[k]), int(r.nobs)

orig = pd.read_csv('results/registered_summary.csv')
orig = orig[orig.analysis_id == 'H1:Misinformation'].iloc[0]

# E1: drop respondents who picked the same screen position in all trials
pos = df.assign(a=(df.profile == 'A').astype(float)).loc[df.chosen_share == 1]
g = pos.groupby('resp_id')['a'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
bad = g.index[(g['count'] >= 3) & (g['mean'].isin([0, 1]))]
sub = df[~df.resp_id.isin(bad)]
b, s, n = amce(sub)
e1 = pd.DataFrame([{'sample': 'registered', 'estimate': orig.estimate, 'se': orig.std_error, 'n': orig.n},
                   {'sample': 'drop position-straightliners', 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n}])
e1.to_csv('results/E1_straightliners.csv', index=False)
print(f'E1 misinfo AMCE {orig.estimate:.3f} -> {b:.3f} (se {orig.std_error:.3f}->{s:.3f}), dropped {len(bad)} resp')

# E2: heterogeneity by age tertile
rows = []
for t in ['Lowest', 'Middle', 'Highest']:
    for arm in ['Misinformation', 'Fact-check']:
        b, s, n = amce(df[df.age_t == t], arm)
        rows.append({'age_tertile': t, 'arm': arm, 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n})
e2 = pd.DataFrame(rows); e2.to_csv('results/E2_age_tertile.csv', index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), facecolor='white')
for arm, c, off in [('Misinformation', '#c0392b', -0.05), ('Fact-check', '#333333', 0.05)]:
    d = e2[e2.arm == arm]; x = np.arange(3) + off
    ax.errorbar(x, d.estimate, yerr=1.96 * d.se, fmt='o', color=c, capsize=0)
    ax.text(2.2, d.estimate.iloc[-1], arm, color=c, va='center')
ax.axhline(0, color='#333333', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(3)); ax.set_xticklabels(['Youngest', 'Middle', 'Oldest'])
ax.set_xlim(-0.4, 3.2); ax.set_ylabel('AMCE on sharing')
for sp in ['top', 'right', 'left']: ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('figures/E2_age_tertile.png', dpi=200)
m = e2[e2.arm == 'Misinformation'].estimate
print(f'E2 misinfo AMCE by age tertile: {m.round(3).tolist()}')
"}

import importlib.util, pathlib
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/clean.csv')
H = [h for h in reg.HYPOTHESES if (h.get('id') or h.get('analysis_id')) == 'H1'][0]
est = H['estimator']; cov = H.get('covariates', [])

def amce(sub, arm='Misinformation'):
    sub = sub.reset_index(drop=True)
    f, d2 = reg.build_formula('share', est, cov, sub)
    d2 = d2.reset_index(drop=True)
    r = reg.fit(d2, f, est)
    k = [i for i in r.params.index if 'arm_code' in i and arm in i][0]
    return float(r.params[k]), float(r.bse[k]), int(r.nobs)

orig = pd.read_csv('results/registered_summary.csv')
orig = orig[orig.analysis_id == 'H1:Misinformation'].iloc[0]

pos = df.assign(a=(df.profile == 'A').astype(float)).loc[df.chosen_share == 1]
g = pos.groupby('resp_id')['a'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
bad = g.index[(g['count'] >= 3) & (g['mean'].isin([0, 1]))]
sub = df[~df.resp_id.isin(bad)]
b, s, n = amce(sub)
e1 = pd.DataFrame([{'sample': 'registered', 'estimate': orig.estimate, 'se': orig.std_error, 'n': orig.n},
                   {'sample': 'drop position-straightliners', 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n}])
e1.to_csv('results/E1_straightliners.csv', index=False)
print(f'E1 misinfo AMCE {orig.estimate:.3f} -> {b:.3f} (se {orig.std_error:.3f}->{s:.3f}), dropped {len(bad)} resp')

rows = []
for t in ['Lowest', 'Middle', 'Highest']:
    for arm in ['Misinformation', 'Fact-check']:
        b, s, n = amce(df[df.age_t == t], arm)
        rows.append({'age_tertile': t, 'arm': arm, 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n})
e2 = pd.DataFrame(rows); e2.to_csv('results/E2_age_tertile.csv', index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), facecolor='white')
for arm, c, off in [('Misinformation', '#c0392b', -0.05), ('Fact-check', '#333333', 0.05)]:
    d = e2[e2.arm == arm]; x = np.arange(3) + off
    ax.errorbar(x, d.estimate, yerr=1.96 * d.se, fmt='o', color=c, capsize=0)
    ax.text(2.2, d.estimate.iloc[-1], arm, color=c, va='center')
ax.axhline(0, color='#333333', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(3)); ax.set_xticklabels(['Youngest', 'Middle', 'Oldest'])
ax.set_xlim(-0.4, 3.2); ax.set_ylabel('AMCE on sharing')
for sp in ['top', 'right', 'left']: ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('figures/E2_age_tertile.png', dpi=200)
m = e2[e2.arm == 'Misinformation'].estimate
print(f'E2 misinfo AMCE by age tertile: {m.round(3).tolist()}')

{"path": "scripts/04_exploratory.py", "content": "import importlib.util, pathlib
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/clean.csv')
H = [h for h in reg.HYPOTHESES if (h.get('id') or h.get('analysis_id')) == 'H1'][0]
est = H['estimator']; cov = H.get('covariates', [])

def amce(sub, arm='Misinformation'):
    f, d2 = reg.build_formula('share', est, cov, sub)
    r = reg.fit(d2, f, est)
    k = [i for i in r.params.index if 'arm_code' in i and arm in i][0]
    return float(r.params[k]), float(r.bse[k]), int(r.nobs)

orig = pd.read_csv('results/registered_summary.csv')
orig = orig[orig.analysis_id == 'H1:Misinformation'].iloc[0]

# E1: drop respondents who picked the same screen position in all trials
pos = df.assign(a=(df.profile == 'A').astype(float)).loc[df.chosen_share == 1]
g = pos.groupby('resp_id')['a'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
bad = g.index[(g['count'] >= 3) & (g['mean'].isin([0, 1]))]
sub = df[~df.resp_id.isin(bad)]
b, s, n = amce(sub)
e1 = pd.DataFrame([{'sample': 'registered', 'estimate': orig.estimate, 'se': orig.std_error, 'n': orig.n},
                   {'sample': 'drop position-straightliners', 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n}])
e1.to_csv('results/E1_straightliners.csv', index=False)
print(f'E1 misinfo AMCE {orig.estimate:.3f} -> {b:.3f} (se {orig.std_error:.3f}->{s:.3f}), dropped {len(bad)} resp')

# E2: heterogeneity by age tertile
rows = []
for t in ['Lowest', 'Middle', 'Highest']:
    for arm in ['Misinformation', 'Fact-check']:
        b, s, n = amce(df[df.age_t == t], arm)
        rows.append({'age_tertile': t, 'arm': arm, 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n})
e2 = pd.DataFrame(rows); e2.to_csv('results/E2_age_tertile.csv', index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), facecolor='white')
for arm, c, off in [('Misinformation', '#c0392b', -0.05), ('Fact-check', '#333333', 0.05)]:
    d = e2[e2.arm == arm]; x = np.arange(3) + off
    ax.errorbar(x, d.estimate, yerr=1.96 * d.se, fmt='o', color=c, capsize=0)
    ax.text(2.2, d.estimate.iloc[-1], arm, color=c, va='center')
ax.axhline(0, color='#333333', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(3)); ax.set_xticklabels(['Youngest', 'Middle', 'Oldest'])
ax.set_xlim(-0.4, 3.2); ax.set_ylabel('AMCE on sharing')
for sp in ['top', 'right', 'left']: ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('figures/E2_age_tertile.png', dpi=200)
m = e2[e2.arm == 'Misinformation'].estimate
print(f'E2 misinfo AMCE by age tertile: {m.round(3).tolist()}')
"}

- R7: AMCE of tie strength on plausibility: each level against 'Distant tie', from the regression of plausibility on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent; re-weighted by the inverse of the realized assignment probability of tie strength (stabilized). (outcome plausibility)
- R8: AMCE of sharer origin on plausibility: each level against 'Foreign origin', from the regression of plausibility on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent; re-weighted by the inverse of the realized assignment probability of sharer origin (stabilized). (outcome plausibility)
- R9: AMCE of sharer ideology on plausibility: each level against 'Liberal sharer', from the regression of plausibility on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent; re-weighted by the inverse of the realized assignment probability of sharer ideology (stabilized). (outcome plausibility)
- R10: AMCE of trust in sharer on plausibility: each level against 'Trust: low', from the regression of plausibility on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent; re-weighted by the inverse of the realized assignment probability of trust in sharer (stabilized). (outcome plausibility)
- R11: AMCE of sharer political knowledge on plausibility: each level against 'Knowledge: low', from the regression of plausibility on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent; re-weighted by the inverse of the realized assignment probability of sharer political knowledge (stabilized). (outcome plausibility)
- R12: AMCE of sharer belief in disputed claims on plausibility: each level against 'Conspiracy belief: low', from the regression of plausibility on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent; re-weighted by the inverse of the realized assignment probability of sharer belief in disputed claims (stabilized). (outcome plausibility)
- X1: A1. Source credibility is conditional on content uncertainty: the slope of sharing on trust in the sharer (1-5), net of the other source attributes, and how it differs by information type. (outcome share)
- X2: A1. The slope of plausibility on trust in the sharer, by information type. (outcome plausibility)
- X3: A1. The close-tie premium on sharing, net of the other source attributes, by information type. (outcome share)
- X4: A2. Sharing without believing: among profiles chosen to share, the probability that the respondent judged the other post more plausible, by information type, net of source attributes, media trust and age. (outcome share_not_believe)
- X5: A3. Co-ideological messenger: sharing when the respondent and the sharer lean the same way (both liberal or both conservative) against opposite leans; pairs involving a moderate form a third group. Cell differences, no controls. (outcome share)
- X6: A4. Ego-network composition: the respondent's six named contacts as a measured network. Among misinformation profiles, sharing on the network's mean perceived belief in disputed claims, net of network ideological spread, mean trust, age and ideology. Each misinformation profile is weighted by 1 / the respondent's number of them, which reproduces the respondent-level regression of the misinformation-sharing rate. (outcome share)
- X7: B1. Message x respondent congruence: among partisan respondents shown partisan-slanted headlines, sharing of congenial against uncongenial content (headline slant from the paper's preliminary automated coding), by information type. (outcome share)
- X8: B2. A conspiracy-prone source: the slope of sharing on the sharer's perceived belief in disputed claims (0-1), net of the other source attributes, by information type. (outcome share)
- X9: B2. The slope of plausibility on the sharer's perceived belief in disputed claims, by information type. (outcome plausibility)
- X10: B2, claim-specific (thin): for the anti-vaccine (polio) misinformation headline, plausibility when the sharer is seen as believing 'Covid-19 vaccines modify your DNA' against not. (outcome plausibility)
- X11: B3. Health vs. political misinformation: among misinformation profiles, the trust slope on sharing for health (guanabana, polio) and political headlines. (outcome share)
- X12: B3. Among misinformation profiles, the close-tie premium for health and political headlines. (outcome share)
- X13: B4. Sharer origin (continental US vs. elsewhere) and sharing, by survey language and by the respondent's nativity. (outcome share)

{"path": "scripts/04_exploratory.py", "content": "import importlib.util, pathlib
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/clean.csv')
H = [h for h in reg.HYPOTHESES if (h.get('id') or h.get('analysis_id')) == 'H1'][0]
est = H['estimator']; cov = H.get('covariates', [])

def amce(sub, arm='Misinformation'):
    f, d2 = reg.build_formula('share', est, cov, sub)
    r = reg.fit(d2, f, est)
    k = [i for i in r.params.index if 'arm_code' in i and arm in i][0]
    return float(r.params[k]), float(r.bse[k]), int(r.nobs)

orig = pd.read_csv('results/registered_summary.csv')
orig = orig[orig.analysis_id == 'H1:Misinformation'].iloc[0]

# E1: drop respondents who picked the same screen position in all trials
pos = df.assign(a=(df.profile == 'A').astype(float)).loc[df.chosen_share == 1]
g = pos.groupby('resp_id')['a'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
bad = g.index[(g['count'] >= 3) & (g['mean'].isin([0, 1]))]
sub = df[~df.resp_id.isin(bad)]
b, s, n = amce(sub)
e1 = pd.DataFrame([{'sample': 'registered', 'estimate': orig.estimate, 'se': orig.std_error, 'n': orig.n},
                   {'sample': 'drop position-straightliners', 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n}])
e1.to_csv('results/E1_straightliners.csv', index=False)
print(f'E1 misinfo AMCE {orig.estimate:.3f} -> {b:.3f} (se {orig.std_error:.3f}->{s:.3f}), dropped {len(bad)} resp')

# E2: heterogeneity by age tertile
rows = []
for t in ['Lowest', 'Middle', 'Highest']:
    for arm in ['Misinformation', 'Fact-check']:
        b, s, n = amce(df[df.age_t == t], arm)
        rows.append({'age_tertile': t, 'arm': arm, 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n})
e2 = pd.DataFrame(rows); e2.to_csv('results/E2_age_tertile.csv', index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), facecolor='white')
for arm, c, off in [('Misinformation', '#c0392b', -0.05), ('Fact-check', '#333333', 0.05)]:
    d = e2[e2.arm == arm]; x = np.arange(3) + off
    ax.errorbar(x, d.estimate, yerr=1.96 * d.se, fmt='o', color=c, capsize=0)
    ax.text(2.2, d.estimate.iloc[-1], arm, color=c, va='center')
ax.axhline(0, color='#333333', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(3)); ax.set_xticklabels(['Youngest', 'Middle', 'Oldest'])
ax.set_xlim(-0.4, 3.2); ax.set_ylabel('AMCE on sharing')
for sp in ['top', 'right', 'left']: ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('figures/E2_age_tertile.png', dpi=200)
m = e2[e2.arm == 'Misinformation'].estimate
print(f'E2 misinfo AMCE by age tertile: {m.round(3).tolist()}')
"}

messages.content:
You are a quantitative social scientist adding a small set of EXPLORATORY analyses (at most three) to a survey experiment whose registered tests are already done. Choose analyses that help interpret the registered results: e.g. effects on component items, robustness to attention-check failures or alternative exclusions, heterogeneity by a demographic the PAP did not register, dose/manipulation checks, or a placebo. Avoid fishing; each analysis must have a one-sentence rationale.

Write ONE script scripts/04_exploratory.py (pandas, statsmodels, matplotlib Agg) that reads data/clean.csv, writes one tidy CSV per analysis to results/E<k>_<slug>.csv and at most two PNG figures to figures/ (minimal style: white background, no top/right/left spines, no gridlines, dark ink, one accent colour at most, direct labels instead of legends, 200 dpi), and prints one summary line per analysis. Use HC2 robust SEs. Run it with run_script; fix errors; then call
record_result(key="exploratory", value=[{"id":"E1","title":str,"rationale":str,"method":str,"table":"results/E1_x.csv","figure":"figures/..png" or null,"finding":one sentence with the key number}], final=true).
Reuse the registered script's helpers instead of writing your own model code. At the top of your script:
    import importlib.util, pathlib
    _spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
Then `formula, d2 = reg.build_formula(outcome, est, covariates, df_subset)` and `res = reg.fit(d2, formula, est)` give exactly the registered model (Lin centring, weights, HC2) on any subset; `reg.HYPOTHESES` holds each hypothesis dict with its `estimator` (use `est = h['estimator']`). For a plain weighted regression of your own, pass weights as a Series: `smf.wls(formula, data=d, weights=d['ipw']).fit(cov_type='HC2')` (never a column name string). Convert any object-typed numeric column with `pd.to_numeric(..., errors='coerce')` before fitting.
Robustness checks of a registered estimate must re-fit the SAME specification as scripts/03_registered.py (same formula, same weights column, same covariates and centring, same HC2 errors) on the alternative sample, and the table must hold both the original and the re-estimated estimate and SE side by side. If a standard error changes by more than a factor of two while the sample changes by less than 10%, your model is misspecified: fix it or drop the analysis.
Never print rows of data. Do not read data files directly.

You have 12 turns. Turn 1: write_file the full script. Turn 2: run_script. Fix and re-run if needed, then record_result with final=true. Record whatever analyses succeeded before you run out of turns.

{"path": "scripts/04_exploratory.py", "content": "import importlib.util, pathlib
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/clean.csv')
H = [h for h in reg.HYPOTHESES if (h.get('id') or h.get('analysis_id')) == 'H1'][0]
est = H['estimator']; cov = H.get('covariates', [])

def amce(sub, arm='Misinformation'):
    f, d2 = reg.build_formula('share', est, cov, sub)
    r = reg.fit(d2, f, est)
    k = [i for i in r.params.index if 'arm_code' in i and arm in i][0]
    return float(r.params[k]), float(r.bse[k]), int(r.nobs)

orig = pd.read_csv('results/registered_summary.csv')
orig = orig[orig.analysis_id == 'H1:Misinformation'].iloc[0]

# E1: drop respondents who picked the same screen position in all trials
pos = df.assign(a=(df.profile == 'A').astype(float)).loc[df.chosen_share == 1]
g = pos.groupby('resp_id')['a'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
bad = g.index[(g['count'] >= 3) & (g['mean'].isin([0, 1]))]
sub = df[~df.resp_id.isin(bad)]
b, s, n = amce(sub)
e1 = pd.DataFrame([{'sample': 'registered', 'estimate': orig.estimate, 'se': orig.std_error, 'n': orig.n},
                   {'sample': 'drop position-straightliners', 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n}])

You are a quantitative social scientist adding a small set of EXPLORATORY analyses (at most three) to a survey experiment whose registered tests are already done. Choose analyses that help interpret the registered results: e.g. effects on component items, robustness to attention-check failures or alternative exclusions, heterogeneity by a demographic the PAP did not register, dose/manipulation checks, or a placebo. Avoid fishing; each analysis must have a one-sentence rationale.

Write ONE script scripts/04_exploratory.py (pandas, statsmodels, matplotlib Agg) that reads data/clean.csv, writes one tidy CSV per analysis to results/E<k>_<slug>.csv and at most two PNG figures to figures/ (minimal style: white background, no top/right/left spines, no gridlines, dark ink, one accent colour at most, direct labels instead of legends, 200 dpi), and prints one summary line per analysis. Use HC2 robust SEs. Run it with run_script; fix errors; then call

Reuse the registered script's helpers instead of writing your own model code. At the top of your script:

For a plain weighted regression of your own, pass weights as a Series: `smf.wls(formula, data=d, weights=d['ipw']).fit(cov_type='HC2')` (never a column name string). Convert any object-typed numeric column with `pd.to_numeric(..., errors='coerce')` before fitting.
Robustness checks of a registered estimate must re-fit the SAME specification as scripts/03_registered.py (same formula, same weights column, same covariates and centring, same HC2 errors) on the alternative sample, and the table must hold both the original and the re-estimated estimate and SE side by side. {"path": "scripts/04_exploratory.py", "content": "import importlib.util, pathlib
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/clean.csv')
H = [h for h in reg.HYPOTHESES if (h.get('id') or h.get('analysis_id')) == 'H1'][0]
est = H['estimator']; cov = H.get('covariates', [])

def amce(sub, arm='Misinformation'):
    f, d2 = reg.build_formula('share', est, cov, sub)
    r = reg.fit(d2, f, est)
    k = [i for i in r.params.index if 'arm_code' in i and arm in i][0]
    return float(r.params[k]), float(r.bse[k]), int(r.nobs)

orig = pd.read_csv('results/registered_summary.csv')
orig = orig[orig.analysis_id == 'H1:Misinformation'].iloc[0]

# E1: drop respondents who picked the same screen position in all trials
pos = df.assign(a=(df.profile == 'A').astype(float)).loc[df.chosen_share == 1]
g = pos.groupby('resp_id')['a'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
bad = g.index[(g['count'] >= 3) & (g['mean'].isin([0, 1]))]
sub = df[~df.resp_id.isin(bad)]
b, s, n = amce(sub)
e1 = pd.DataFrame([{'sample': 'registered', 'estimate': orig.estimate, 'se': orig.std_error, 'n': orig.n},
                   {'sample': 'drop position-straightliners', 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n}])
e1.to_csv('results/E1_straightliners.csv', index=False)
print(f'E1 misinfo AMCE {orig.estimate:.3f} -> {b:.3f} (se {orig.std_error:.3f}->{s:.3f}), dropped {len(bad)} resp')

# E2: heterogeneity by age tertile
rows = []
for t in ['Lowest', 'Middle', 'Highest']:
    for arm in ['Misinformation', 'Fact-check']:
        b, s, n = amce(df[df.age_t == t], arm)
        rows.append({'age_tertile': t, 'arm': arm, 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n})
e2 = pd.DataFrame(rows); e2.to_csv('results/E2_age_tertile.csv', index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), facecolor='white')
for arm, c, off in [('Misinformation', '#c0392b', -0.05), ('Fact-check', '#333333', 0.05)]:
    d = e2[e2.arm == arm]; x = np.arange(3) + off
    ax.errorbar(x, d.estimate, yerr=1.96 * d.se, fmt='o', color=c, capsize=0)
    ax.text(2.2, d.estimate.iloc[-1], arm, color=c, va='center')
ax.axhline(0, color='#333333', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(3)); ax.set_xticklabels(['Youngest', 'Middle', 'Oldest'])
ax.set_xlim(-0.4, 3.2); ax.set_ylabel('AMCE on sharing')
for sp in ['top', 'right', 'left']: ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('figures/E2_age_tertile.png', dpi=200)
m = e2[e2.arm == 'Misinformation'].estimate
print(f'E2 misinfo AMCE by age tertile: {m.round(3).tolist()}')
"}

function.description: Hand a structured result to the orchestrator. Set final=true when your task is complete.

messages.content:
You are a quantitative social scientist adding a small set of EXPLORATORY analyses (at most three) to a survey experiment whose registered tests are already done. Choose analyses that help interpret the registered results: e.g. effects on component items, robustness to attention-check failures or alternative exclusions, heterogeneity by a demographic the PAP did not register, dose/manipulation checks, or a placebo. Avoid fishing; each analysis must have a one-sentence rationale.

Write ONE script scripts/04_exploratory.py (pandas, statsmodels, matplotlib Agg) that reads data/clean.csv, writes one tidy CSV per analysis to results/E<k>_<slug>.csv and at most two PNG figures to figures/ (minimal style: white background, no top/right/left spines, no gridlines, dark ink, one accent colour at most, direct labels instead of legends, 200 dpi), and prints one summary line per analysis. Use HC2 robust SEs. Run it with run_script; fix errors; then call
record_result(key="exploratory", value=[{"id":"E1","title":str,"rationale":str,"method":str,"table":"results/E1_x.csv","figure":"figures/..png" or null,"finding":one sentence with the key number}], final=true).
Reuse the registered script's helpers instead of writing your own model code. At the top of your script:
    import importlib.util, pathlib
    _spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
Then `formula, d2 = reg.build_formula(outcome, est, covariates, df_subset)` and `res = reg.fit(d2, formula, est)` give exactly the registered model (Lin centring, weights, HC2) on any subset; `reg.HYPOTHESES` holds each hypothesis dict with its `estimator` (use `est = h['estimator']`). {"path": "scripts/04_exploratory.py", "content": "import importlib.util, pathlib
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/clean.csv')
H = [h for h in reg.HYPOTHESES if (h.get('id') or h.get('analysis_id')) == 'H1'][0]
est = H['estimator']; cov = H.get('covariates', [])

def amce(sub, arm='Misinformation'):
    f, d2 = reg.build_formula('share', est, cov, sub)
    r = reg.fit(d2, f, est)
    k = [i for i in r.params.index if 'arm_code' in i and arm in i][0]
    return float(r.params[k]), float(r.bse[k]), int(r.nobs)

orig = pd.read_csv('results/registered_summary.csv')
orig = orig[orig.analysis_id == 'H1:Misinformation'].iloc[0]

# E1: drop respondents who picked the same screen position in all trials
pos = df.assign(a=(df.profile == 'A').astype(float)).loc[df.chosen_share == 1]
g = pos.groupby('resp_id')['a'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
bad = g.index[(g['count'] >= 3) & (g['mean'].isin([0, 1]))]
sub = df[~df.resp_id.isin(bad)]
b, s, n = amce(sub)
e1 = pd.DataFrame([{'sample': 'registered', 'estimate': orig.estimate, 'se': orig.std_error, 'n': orig.n},
                   {'sample': 'drop position-straightliners', 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n}])
e1.to_csv('results/E1_straightliners.csv', index=False)
print(f'E1 misinfo AMCE {orig.estimate:.3f} -> {b:.3f} (se {orig.std_error:.3f}->{s:.3f}), dropped {len(bad)} resp')

# E2: heterogeneity by age tertile
rows = []
for t in ['Lowest', 'Middle', 'Highest']:
    for arm in ['Misinformation', 'Fact-check']:
        b, s, n = amce(df[df.age_t == t], arm)
        rows.append({'age_tertile': t, 'arm': arm, 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n})
e2 = pd.DataFrame(rows); e2.to_csv('results/E2_age_tertile.csv', index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), facecolor='white')
for arm, c, off in [('Misinformation', '#c0392b', -0.05), ('Fact-check', '#333333', 0.05)]:
    d = e2[e2.arm == arm]; x = np.arange(3) + off
    ax.errorbar(x, d.estimate, yerr=1.96 * d.se, fmt='o', color=c, capsize=0)
    ax.text(2.2, d.estimate.iloc[-1], arm, color=c, va='center')
ax.axhline(0, color='#333333', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(3)); ax.set_xticklabels(['Youngest', 'Middle', 'Oldest'])
ax.set_xlim(-0.4, 3.2); ax.set_ylabel('AMCE on sharing')
for sp in ['top', 'right', 'left']: ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('figures/E2_age_tertile.png', dpi=200)
m = e2[e2.arm == 'Misinformation'].estimate
print(f'E2 misinfo AMCE by age tertile: {m.round(3).tolist()}')
"}

{"path": "scripts/04_exploratory.py", "content": "import importlib.util, pathlib
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/clean.csv')
H = [h for h in reg.HYPOTHESES if (h.get('id') or h.get('analysis_id')) == 'H1'][0]
est = H['estimator']; cov = H.get('covariates', [])

def amce(sub, arm='Misinformation'):
    f, d2 = reg.build_formula('share', est, cov, sub)
    r = reg.fit(d2, f, est)
    k = [i for i in r.params.index if 'arm_code' in i and arm in i][0]
    return float(r.params[k]), float(r.bse[k]), int(r.nobs)

orig = pd.read_csv('results/registered_summary.csv')
orig = orig[orig.analysis_id == 'H1:Misinformation'].iloc[0]

# E1: drop respondents who picked the same screen position in all trials
pos = df.assign(a=(df.profile == 'A').astype(float)).loc[df.chosen_share == 1]
g = pos.groupby('resp_id')['a'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
bad = g.index[(g['count'] >= 3) & (g['mean'].isin([0, 1]))]
sub = df[~df.resp_id.isin(bad)]
b, s, n = amce(sub)
e1 = pd.DataFrame([{'sample': 'registered', 'estimate': orig.estimate, 'se': orig.std_error, 'n': orig.n},
                   {'sample': 'drop position-straightliners', 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n}])
e1.to_csv('results/E1_straightliners.csv', index=False)
print(f'E1 misinfo AMCE {orig.estimate:.3f} -> {b:.3f} (se {orig.std_error:.3f}->{s:.3f}), dropped {len(bad)} resp')

# E2: heterogeneity by age tertile
rows = []
for t in ['Lowest', 'Middle', 'Highest']:
    for arm in ['Misinformation', 'Fact-check']:
        b, s, n = amce(df[df.age_t == t], arm)
        rows.append({'age_tertile': t, 'arm': arm, 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n})
e2 = pd.DataFrame(rows); e2.to_csv('results/E2_age_tertile.csv', index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), facecolor='white')
for arm, c, off in [('Misinformation', '#c0392b', -0.05), ('Fact-check', '#333333', 0.05)]:
    d = e2[e2.arm == arm]; x = np.arange(3) + off
    ax.errorbar(x, d.estimate, yerr=1.96 * d.se, fmt='o', color=c, capsize=0)
    ax.text(2.2, d.estimate.iloc[-1], arm, color=c, va='center')
ax.axhline(0, color='#333333', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(3)); ax.set_xticklabels(['Youngest', 'Middle', 'Oldest'])
ax.set_xlim(-0.4, 3.2); ax.set_ylabel('AMCE on sharing')
for sp in ['top', 'right', 'left']: ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('figures/E2_age_tertile.png', dpi=200)
m = e2[e2.arm == 'Misinformation'].estimate
print(f'E2 misinfo AMCE by age tertile: {m.round(3).tolist()}')
"}

messages.content:
You are a quantitative social scientist adding a small set of EXPLORATORY analyses (at most three) to a survey experiment whose registered tests are already done. Choose analyses that help interpret the registered results: e.g. effects on component items, robustness to attention-check failures or alternative exclusions, heterogeneity by a demographic the PAP did not register, dose/manipulation checks, or a placebo. Avoid fishing; each analysis must have a one-sentence rationale.

Write ONE script scripts/04_exploratory.py (pandas, statsmodels, matplotlib Agg) that reads data/clean.csv, writes one tidy CSV per analysis to results/E<k>_<slug>.csv and at most two PNG figures to figures/ (minimal style: white background, no top/right/left spines, no gridlines, dark ink, one accent colour at most, direct labels instead of legends, 200 dpi), and prints one summary line per analysis. Use HC2 robust SEs. Run it with run_script; fix errors; then call
record_result(key="exploratory", value=[{"id":"E1","title":str,"rationale":str,"method":str,"table":"results/E1_x.csv","figure":"figures/..png" or null,"finding":one sentence with the key number}], final=true).
Reuse the registered script's helpers instead of writing your own model code. At the top of your script:
    import importlib.util, pathlib
    _spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
Then `formula, d2 = reg.build_formula(outcome, est, covariates, df_subset)` and `res = reg.fit(d2, formula, est)` give exactly the registered model (Lin centring, weights, HC2) on any subset; `reg.HYPOTHESES` holds each hypothesis dict with its `estimator` (use `est = h['estimator']`). For a plain weighted regression of your own, pass weights as a Series: `smf.wls(formula, data=d, weights=d['ipw']).fit(cov_type='HC2')` (never a column name string). Convert any object-typed numeric column with `pd.to_numeric(..., errors='coerce')` before fitting.
Robustness checks of a registered estimate must re-fit the SAME specification as scripts/03_registered.py (same formula, same weights column, same covariates and centring, same HC2 errors) on the alternative sample, and the table must hold both the original and the re-estimated estimate and SE side by side. If a standard error changes by more than a factor of two while the sample changes by less than 10%, your model is misspecified: fix it or drop the analysis.
Never print rows of data. Do not read data files directly.

You have 12 turns. Turn 1: write_file the full script. Turn 2: run_script. Fix and re-run if needed, then record_result with final=true. Record whatever analyses succeeded before you run out of turns.

{"path": "scripts/04_exploratory.py", "content": "import importlib.util, pathlib
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/clean.csv')
H = [h for h in reg.HYPOTHESES if (h.get('id') or h.get('analysis_id')) == 'H1'][0]
est = H['estimator']; cov = H.get('covariates', [])

def amce(sub, arm='Misinformation'):
    f, d2 = reg.build_formula('share', est, cov, sub)
    r = reg.fit(d2, f, est)
    k = [i for i in r.params.index if 'arm_code' in i and arm in i][0]
    return float(r.params[k]), float(r.bse[k]), int(r.nobs)

orig = pd.read_csv('results/registered_summary.csv')
orig = orig[orig.analysis_id == 'H1:Misinformation'].iloc[0]

# E1: drop respondents who picked the same screen position in all trials
pos = df.assign(a=(df.profile == 'A').astype(float)).loc[df.chosen_share == 1]
g = pos.groupby('resp_id')['a'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
bad = g.index[(g['count'] >= 3) & (g['mean'].isin([0, 1]))]
sub = df[~df.resp_id.isin(bad)]
b, s, n = amce(sub)
e1 = pd.DataFrame([{'sample': 'registered', 'estimate': orig.estimate, 'se': orig.std_error, 'n': orig.n},
                   {'sample': 'drop position-straightliners', 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n}])
e1.to_csv('results/E1_straightliners.csv', index=False)
print(f'E1 misinfo AMCE {orig.estimate:.3f} -> {b:.3f} (se {orig.std_error:.3f}->{s:.3f}), dropped {len(bad)} resp')

# E2: heterogeneity by age tertile
rows = []
for t in ['Lowest', 'Middle', 'Highest']:
    for arm in ['Misinformation', 'Fact-check']:
        b, s, n = amce(df[df.age_t == t], arm)
        rows.append({'age_tertile': t, 'arm': arm, 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n})
e2 = pd.DataFrame(rows); e2.to_csv('results/E2_age_tertile.csv', index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), facecolor='white')
for arm, c, off in [('Misinformation', '#c0392b', -0.05), ('Fact-check', '#333333', 0.05)]:
    d = e2[e2.arm == arm]; x = np.arange(3) + off
    ax.errorbar(x, d.estimate, yerr=1.96 * d.se, fmt='o', color=c, capsize=0)
    ax.text(2.2, d.estimate.iloc[-1], arm, color=c, va='center')
ax.axhline(0, color='#333333', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(3)); ax.set_xticklabels(['Youngest', 'Middle', 'Oldest'])
ax.set_xlim(-0.4, 3.2); ax.set_ylabel('AMCE on sharing')
for sp in ['top', 'right', 'left']: ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('figures/E2_age_tertile.png', dpi=200)
m = e2[e2.arm == 'Misinformation'].estimate
print(f'E2 misinfo AMCE by age tertile: {m.round(3).tolist()}')
"}

{"path": "scripts/04_exploratory.py", "content": "import importlib.util, pathlib
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/clean.csv')
H = [h for h in reg.HYPOTHESES if (h.get('id') or h.get('analysis_id')) == 'H1'][0]
est = H['estimator']; cov = H.get('covariates', [])

def amce(sub, arm='Misinformation'):
    f, d2 = reg.build_formula('share', est, cov, sub)
    r = reg.fit(d2, f, est)
    k = [i for i in r.params.index if 'arm_code' in i and arm in i][0]
    return float(r.params[k]), float(r.bse[k]), int(r.nobs)

orig = pd.read_csv('results/registered_summary.csv')
orig = orig[orig.analysis_id == 'H1:Misinformation'].iloc[0]

# E1: drop respondents who picked the same screen position in all trials
pos = df.assign(a=(df.profile == 'A').astype(float)).loc[df.chosen_share == 1]
g = pos.groupby('resp_id')['a'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
bad = g.index[(g['count'] >= 3) & (g['mean'].isin([0, 1]))]
sub = df[~df.resp_id.isin(bad)]
b, s, n = amce(sub)
e1 = pd.DataFrame([{'sample': 'registered', 'estimate': orig.estimate, 'se': orig.std_error, 'n': orig.n},
                   {'sample': 'drop position-straightliners', 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n}])
e1.to_csv('results/E1_straightliners.csv', index=False)
print(f'E1 misinfo AMCE {orig.estimate:.3f} -> {b:.3f} (se {orig.std_error:.3f}->{s:.3f}), dropped {len(bad)} resp')

# E2: heterogeneity by age tertile
rows = []
for t in ['Lowest', 'Middle', 'Highest']:
    for arm in ['Misinformation', 'Fact-check']:
        b, s, n = amce(df[df.age_t == t], arm)
        rows.append({'age_tertile': t, 'arm': arm, 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n})
e2 = pd.DataFrame(rows); e2.to_csv('results/E2_age_tertile.csv', index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), facecolor='white')
for arm, c, off in [('Misinformation', '#c0392b', -0.05), ('Fact-check', '#333333', 0.05)]:
    d = e2[e2.arm == arm]; x = np.arange(3) + off
    ax.errorbar(x, d.estimate, yerr=1.96 * d.se, fmt='o', color=c, capsize=0)
    ax.text(2.2, d.estimate.iloc[-1], arm, color=c, va='center')
ax.axhline(0, color='#333333', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(3)); ax.set_xticklabels(['Youngest', 'Middle', 'Oldest'])
ax.set_xlim(-0.4, 3.2); ax.set_ylabel('AMCE on sharing')
for sp in ['top', 'right', 'left']: ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('figures/E2_age_tertile.png', dpi=200)
m = e2[e2.arm == 'Misinformation'].estimate
print(f'E2 misinfo AMCE by age tertile: {m.round(3).tolist()}')
"}

messages.content:
You are a quantitative social scientist adding a small set of EXPLORATORY analyses (at most three) to a survey experiment whose registered tests are already done. Choose analyses that help interpret the registered results: e.g. effects on component items, robustness to attention-check failures or alternative exclusions, heterogeneity by a demographic the PAP did not register, dose/manipulation checks, or a placebo. Avoid fishing; each analysis must have a one-sentence rationale.

Write ONE script scripts/04_exploratory.py (pandas, statsmodels, matplotlib Agg) that reads data/clean.csv, writes one tidy CSV per analysis to results/E<k>_<slug>.csv and at most two PNG figures to figures/ (minimal style: white background, no top/right/left spines, no gridlines, dark ink, one accent colour at most, direct labels instead of legends, 200 dpi), and prints one summary line per analysis. Use HC2 robust SEs. Run it with run_script; fix errors; then call
record_result(key="exploratory", value=[{"id":"E1","title":str,"rationale":str,"method":str,"table":"results/E1_x.csv","figure":"figures/..png" or null,"finding":one sentence with the key number}], final=true).
Reuse the registered script's helpers instead of writing your own model code. At the top of your script:
    import importlib.util, pathlib
    _spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
Then `formula, d2 = reg.build_formula(outcome, est, covariates, df_subset)` and `res = reg.fit(d2, formula, est)` give exactly the registered model (Lin centring, weights, HC2) on any subset; `reg.HYPOTHESES` holds each hypothesis dict with its `estimator` (use `est = h['estimator']`). For a plain weighted regression of your own, pass weights as a Series: `smf.wls(formula, data=d, weights=d['ipw']).fit(cov_type='HC2')` (never a column name string). Convert any object-typed numeric column with `pd.to_numeric(..., errors='coerce')` before fitting.
Robustness checks of a registered estimate must re-fit the SAME specification as scripts/03_registered.py (same formula, same weights column, same covariates and centring, same HC2 errors) on the alternative sample, and the table must hold both the original and the re-estimated estimate and SE side by side. If a standard error changes by more than a factor of two while the sample changes by less than 10%, your model is misspecified: fix it or drop the analysis.
Never print rows of data. Do not read data files directly.

- X4: A2. Sharing without believing: among profiles chosen to share, the probability that the respondent judged the other post more plausible, by information type, net of source attributes, media trust and age. (outcome share_not_believe)
- X5: A3. Co-ideological messenger: sharing when the respondent and the sharer lean the same way (both liberal or both conservative) against opposite leans; pairs involving a moderate form a third group. Cell differences, no controls. (outcome share)
- X6: A4. Ego-network composition: the respondent's six named contacts as a measured network. Among misinformation profiles, sharing on the network's mean perceived belief in disputed claims, net of network ideological spread, mean trust, age and ideology. - X7: B1. Message x respondent congruence: among partisan respondents shown partisan-slanted headlines, sharing of congenial against uncongenial content (headline slant from the paper's preliminary automated coding), by information type. (outcome share)

- X11: B3. Health vs. political misinformation: among misinformation profiles, the trust slope on sharing for health (guanabana, polio) and political headlines. (outcome share)
- X12: B3. Among misinformation profiles, the close-tie premium for health and political headlines. (outcome share)

{"path": "scripts/04_exploratory.py", "content": "import importlib.util, pathlib
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('reg', pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('03_registered.py')); reg = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec); _spec.loader.exec_module(reg)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv('data/clean.csv')
H = [h for h in reg.HYPOTHESES if (h.get('id') or h.get('analysis_id')) == 'H1'][0]
est = H['estimator']; cov = H.get('covariates', [])

def amce(sub, arm='Misinformation'):
    f, d2 = reg.build_formula('share', est, cov, sub)
    r = reg.fit(d2, f, est)
    k = [i for i in r.params.index if 'arm_code' in i and arm in i][0]
    return float(r.params[k]), float(r.bse[k]), int(r.nobs)

orig = pd.read_csv('results/registered_summary.csv')
orig = orig[orig.analysis_id == 'H1:Misinformation'].iloc[0]

# E1: drop respondents who picked the same screen position in all trials
pos = df.assign(a=(df.profile == 'A').astype(float)).loc[df.chosen_share == 1]
g = pos.groupby('resp_id')['a'].agg(['mean', 'count'])
bad = g.index[(g['count'] >= 3) & (g['mean'].isin([0, 1]))]
sub = df[~df.resp_id.isin(bad)]
b, s, n = amce(sub)
e1 = pd.DataFrame([{'sample': 'registered', 'estimate': orig.estimate, 'se': orig.std_error, 'n': orig.n},
                   {'sample': 'drop position-straightliners', 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n}])
e1.to_csv('results/E1_straightliners.csv', index=False)
print(f'E1 misinfo AMCE {orig.estimate:.3f} -> {b:.3f} (se {orig.std_error:.3f}->{s:.3f}), dropped {len(bad)} resp')

# E2: heterogeneity by age tertile
rows = []
for t in ['Lowest', 'Middle', 'Highest']:
    for arm in ['Misinformation', 'Fact-check']:
        b, s, n = amce(df[df.age_t == t], arm)
        rows.append({'age_tertile': t, 'arm': arm, 'estimate': b, 'se': s, 'n': n})
e2 = pd.DataFrame(rows); e2.to_csv('results/E2_age_tertile.csv', index=False)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5), facecolor='white')
for arm, c, off in [('Misinformation', '#c0392b', -0.05), ('Fact-check', '#333333', 0.05)]:
    d = e2[e2.arm == arm]; x = np.arange(3) + off
    ax.errorbar(x, d.estimate, yerr=1.96 * d.se, fmt='o', color=c, capsize=0)
    ax.text(2.2, d.estimate.iloc[-1], arm, color=c, va='center')
ax.axhline(0, color='#333333', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xticks(range(3)); ax.set_xticklabels(['Youngest', 'Middle', 'Oldest'])
ax.set_xlim(-0.4, 3.2); ax.set_ylabel('AMCE on sharing')
for sp in ['top', 'right', 'left']: ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
ax.grid(False)
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('figures/E2_age_tertile.png', dpi=200)
m = e2[e2.arm == 'Misinformation'].estimate
print(f'E2 misinfo AMCE by age tertile: {m.round(3).tolist()}')
"}

- X12: B3. Among misinformation profiles, the close-tie premium for health and political headlines.
- X13: B4. Sharer origin (continental US vs. elsewhere) and sharing, by survey language and by the respondent's nativity.

messages.content:
You write the narrative sections of a short research report on an unpublished conjoint experiment, for a reader who knows social science but has not seen the study. You receive the hypotheses with their tags (registered / deviation / exploratory), the result tables, exploratory findings, and a literature note. The report skeleton already prints the model formulas, the full tables, a key-findings table and the figures; your job is the prose around them.

Voice: a careful colleague explaining the study to a peer, not a form being filled in. Vary sentence openings; do not begin the summary and the design notes the same way; do not restate the hypothesis sentence that already sits under each heading; say "significant" once per section at most and otherwise let the interval speak.

Style:
- Plain, legible English. Short paragraphs (2-4 sentences). One idea per sentence. Lead with what was found, then how.
- Refer to arms and outcomes by their labels (e.g. "Automated Flagging", "total accuracy"), never by codes or column names. Do not paste formulas, column names, variable codes or file paths into prose; they are shown separately.
- For an outcome on a 0-1 proportion scale, state effects in percentage points ("4.4 points higher", from +0.044) and give the raw estimate once in parentheses if useful. Give a 95% CI for each effect you name.
- Name the significant effects with their CI and p-value; summarise the rest in one sentence ("the other eight arms were within about ±3 points of control and not distinguishable from it"). Do not list every arm's numbers.
- Numbers must come from the tables. Never add results that are not in the tables.
- A non-significant estimate is inconclusive, not evidence of no effect. Never write "had no effect", "did not change" or "neither improved nor harmed"; say it was not distinguishable from zero and give the CI.
- Cite the p-value that matches the hypothesis (`p_directional`, one-sided for a stated direction, when present) and say whether it is one- or two-sided, once.
- Mention the sample flow once, in the design notes: raw N, analysis N, and any rows dropped for missing values (`n_eligible` vs model `n`), plus the control-group size.
- If the plan was not pre-registered (registration status "none"), say once, plainly, that every test is post hoc, and never call an analysis "registered" or "pre-specified". If an analysis carries a deviation tag, say in one sentence what changed and why it matters (or does not).
- Exploratory results (E1, E2, ...) come from model-written code that nobody has reviewed. Report them only in their own section and in at most one takeaway, introduced as exploratory. Never let an exploratory result overturn, qualify or cast doubt on a registered result in the abstract or the registered results; if an exploratory check disagrees with a registered estimate, say in the exploratory section that the two disagree and that the check is unreviewed.
- Do not overclaim: p-values near the threshold, small arms and many uncorrected tests all deserve a hedge, stated once.
- No headings, no bullet lists, no bold, no markdown tables inside your sections; plain paragraphs only.

Takeaways: 3 to 5 bullets for a reader who will read nothing else. Each is one or two plain sentences, at most 30 words, with one number at most (the effect in natural units with its CI or p-value). The first bullet answers the research question; the middle ones give the findings that matter, saying "registered" or "exploratory" where it changes the reading; the last gives the main caveat (multiple uncorrected tests, small arms, post hoc). No codes, no column names, no lists of every arm. Every claim names its outcome. Words like "performance", "outcomes" or "anything" are not outcomes. Superlatives ("the only arm to...", "the largest effect") are allowed only for one named outcome and only if the Key numbers block confirms them (bad: "the only registered arm to harm performance"; good: "the only arm that lowered accuracy"). When an effect is negative, write the CI of the effect itself, e.g. −3.9 points (95% CI [−7.4, −0.3]), never a flipped-sign interval. Use the "Key numbers" block for the figures. Write "p < 0.001" for any p-value below 0.001, never "p = 0.000".

Abstract: one paragraph, 120 to 170 words, in the order a journal abstract uses: the question, the design and sample in one sentence, the main results with their numbers, and one sentence of caveat. It must stand alone when shared without the rest of the report.

Length: abstract ≤ 170 words; design_notes ≤ 120 words; each result note ≤ 110 words; each exploratory note ≤ 60 words; limitations ≤ 150 words.

Return ONLY JSON:
{"takeaways": [str, ...], "abstract": str, "design_notes": str, "results": {"H1": str, "H2": str, "S1": str, ...}, "exploratory": {"E1": str, ...}, "limitations": str}

## Literature note
The retrieved list is thin and mostly off-topic, so it says little directly about the hypotheses on source cues (tie strength, origin, ideology, trust, knowledge, conspiracy belief) and information type in sharing and plausibility. The closest items are general. Lewandowsky et al. (2017) discuss how misinformation spreads and influences people, and Roozenbeek et al. (2020) report predictors of belief in COVID-19 misinformation across countries, including links to health behaviours. Neither tests how sharer attributes shape sharing or plausibility, so neither bears on the AMCE estimates for H1-H14 or the weighted robustness checks R1-R12. Van Bavel et al. (2020) is a broad pandemic-response review with no abstract available. Three retrieved works are unrelated to the hypotheses: Dwivedi et al. (2019) on AI, Jenkins and Purushotma (2006) on media education, and Kniffin et al. (2020) on workplaces. The EMNLP 2021 proceedings entry (2021) is also unrelated. The works tagged as method concern attitudes toward the unvaccinated (Bor et al., 2022), election-lie acceptance (Arceneaux & Truex, 2022), and a vaccine-hesitancy survey with embedded conjoint experiments (Stamm et al., 2022). Only the last is a design precedent, as another conjoint on a health topic, and its abstract snippet reports no findings relevant here.

The retrieved works do not clearly disagree with each other or with the study's expectations, because none reports findings on the specific source-cue effects. The one tension is loose. Lewandowsky et al. (2017) frame misinformation as a broad societal problem, while Roozenbeek et al. (2020) locate susceptibility in individual and country-level predictors. Neither speaks to whether sharing depends on who shares, or to sharing without believing (X4). The study's conjoint design, which randomizes source attributes and measures both sharing and plausibility, can speak to that question directly, but the retrieved literature offers no benchmark against which to compare the estimates.

Each hypothesis with arms is one profile feature: the "arms" are its levels and the "control" is its reference level, so each
estimate is an AMCE (the change in the probability that a profile is chosen when the feature takes that level instead of the
reference, averaging over the other features). Write "levels" and "reference level", not "arms" and "control group".
Subgroup tables with columns mm_<group> and difference are differences in marginal means (the share of profiles with that
level that were chosen) between two respondent groups; name the levels whose difference is distinguishable from zero.

other features.

## Report
# Who Shares What From Whom: An Ego-Network Conjoint of Misinformation Sharing

*Yamil R. Velez · 2026-10-07 · N = 12,000 analysed of 12,000 collected · conjoint experiment*

<!-- fd:badges -->
![provenance: fully agentic](figures/badges/provenance.svg) ![review: unreviewed](figures/badges/review.svg) [![plan: pre-registered #132,508](figures/badges/registration.svg)](https://aspredicted.org/8njc-mpqw.pdf) ![status: draft](figures/badges/release.svg) ![design: conjoint](figures/badges/design.svg) ![data: open data](figures/badges/data.svg) ![model calls: $0.00](figures/badges/cost.svg)

Who Shares What From Whom: An Ego-Network Conjoint of Misinformation Sharing [Unpublished study package, generated with filedrawer 0.1.0]. The File Drawer. https://github.com/yrvelez/fact-networks-conjoint

<!-- fd:section id=abstract -->
## Abstract

Who shares misinformation, and from whom? We ran a registered conjoint experiment with a YouGov sample of US respondents (12,000 profile ratings). Each respondent saw a true or neutral headline, a false headline, or a fact-check, attributed to one of their real contacts, and chose whether to share it and rated its plausibility. Information type was randomized. Misinformation was chosen for sharing 18.2 points less often than true or neutral headlines (95% CI [−20.4, −16.0]), and fact-checks 13.3 points less often (95% CI [−15.6, −11.1]). Plausibility showed a similar pattern. Among the measured source attributes, close ties (+3.0 points, 95% CI [1.0, 5.0]) and high trust in the sharer (+5.7 points, 95% CI [2.3, 9.1]) raised sharing, while origin, knowledge and conspiracy belief were not distinguishable from zero. Respondents with greater belief in disputed claims shared misinformation more. Caveats: many uncorrected tests, and the source attributes are measured, not randomized.

<!-- fd:section id=findings -->
## Key findings

- In this registered conjoint, information type shaped sharing most: misinformation headlines were chosen 18.2 points less often than true/neutral ones (95% CI [−20.4, −16.0], p < 0.001).
- Fact-check headlines were also chosen less often than true/neutral ones, by 13.3 points (95% CI [−15.6, −11.1]). Plausibility ratings tracked sharing closely.
- Among measured sharer attributes, close ties raised sharing by 3.0 points (95% CI [1.0, 5.0]) and high trust by 5.7 points (95% CI [2.3, 9.1]); origin, knowledge and conspiracy belief were not distinguishable from zero.
- Registered subgroups showed that respondents with higher belief in disputed claims shared misinformation 5.6 points more than those with lower belief (p < 0.001), and true/neutral content less.
- Many tests were run without correction, sharer attributes are measured rather than randomized, and the ideology and subgroup findings sit near conventional thresholds.

<!-- fd:section id=design -->
## Design and data

A conjoint experiment with 7 profile features: randomized, Information type (True/neutral, Misinformation, Fact-check); measured rather than randomized (the respondent's own ratings of the real contact each headline was attributed to; only the headline and its assignment to a contact are randomized), Tie strength (Distant tie, Close tie); Sharer origin (Foreign origin, Continental US); Sharer ideology (Liberal sharer, Moderate sharer, Conservative sharer); Trust in sharer (Trust: low, Trust: mid, Trust: high); Sharer political knowledge (Knowledge: low, Knowledge: mid, Knowledge: high); Sharer belief in disputed claims (Conspiracy belief: low, Conspiracy belief: high); yougov, US. 12,000 responses were collected and 12,000 are analysed. The plan is pre-registered at https://aspredicted.org/8njc-mpqw.pdf. Identifier and free-text columns removed before any model saw the data: none.

![Design at a glance](figures/design.svg)

#### Details: the design in words

A conjoint experiment on yougov respondents in US (N = 12,000 analysed). Each profile is built from 7 features: Information type (True/neutral, Misinformation, Fact-check); Tie strength (Distant tie, Close tie; measured, not randomized); Sharer origin (Foreign origin, Continental US; measured, not randomized); Sharer ideology (Liberal sharer, Moderate sharer, Conservative sharer; measured, not randomized); Trust in sharer (Trust: low, Trust: mid, Trust: high; measured, not randomized); Sharer political knowledge (Knowledge: low, Knowledge: mid, Knowledge: high; measured, not randomized); Sharer belief in disputed claims (Conspiracy belief: low, Conspiracy belief: high; measured, not randomized). Respondents compare two profiles per task and choose one for each outcome. Outcomes: Chosen to share, Chosen as more plausible. Registered moderators: age_t, ideo_self_t, disp_self_t, media_t, survey_language.


Respondents were a YouGov sample of US adults, and the analysis used all 12,000 raw profile ratings, with none dropped for missing values on the main outcomes. Each profile attributed a headline to one of the respondent's real contacts. Only the headline type and its assignment to a contact were randomized. Tie strength, origin, ideology, trust, knowledge and conspiracy belief are measured attributes of those contacts, so their AMCEs are descriptive contrasts that bundle correlated attributes, not causal effects. True/neutral headlines are the reference level for information type (3,854 misinformation and 3,972 fact-check profiles were eligible). Standard errors are clustered by respondent, and tests are two-sided.

<!-- fd:section id=results -->
## Results

![Effects of every profile feature on chosen to share (AMCEs, 95% CI)](figures/amce_share.png)

![Effects of every profile feature on chosen as more plausible (AMCEs, 95% CI)](figures/amce_plausibility.png)

<!-- fd:hyp id=H1 tag=registered outcome=share -->
### H1. Information type → sharing

*AMCE of information type on sharing: each level against 'True/neutral', from the regression of sharing on all seven profile features, SEs clustered by respondent.*  
*Pre-registered.*

Information type had large effects on sharing. Misinformation was chosen 18.2 points less often than true or neutral headlines (95% CI [−20.4, −16.0], p < 0.001), and fact-checks 13.3 points less often (95% CI [−15.6, −11.1], p < 0.001). Chosen shares were 60.3% for true/neutral, 42.1% for misinformation and 47.0% for fact-checks. These are causal contrasts, because headline type was randomized.

#### Details: model and estimates by arm (H1)

```
share ~ C(arm_code, Treatment(reference='True/neutral')) + C(tie) + C(sharer_origin) + C(sharer_ideology) + C(sharer_trust) + C(sharer_knowledge) + C(sharer_conspiracy)
OLS | cluster-robust SEs on resp_id | N = 11882 | two-sided test, alpha = 0.05
```
